## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Uppādavāra* ("Section on Arising" or "Origination") is the first subsection of the *pavattivāra* (the process or explanation section, also termed *niddesavāra*) of the *Sacca-yamaka*, the fifth book of the Abhidhamma treatise *Yamaka* [Anderson 1999; Nyanatiloka 1957; Ronkin 2005]. In this section, the text analyzes the four noble truths (*ariya-sacca*) in dynamic terms, examining whether and how the arising of one truth implies the arising of another truth [Anderson 1999]. These inquiries are systematically pursued with respect to persons (*puggala*), places of rebirth (*okāsa*), and persons and places together, across the temporal modes of present, past, and future, in both positive (*anuloma*) and negative (*paccanīka*) formulations [Anderson 1999; Nyanatiloka 1957]. This systematic analysis belongs to the broader Yamaka framework that analyzes doctrinal categories through origination (*uppāda-vāra*), cessation (*nirodha-vāra*), and origination-cessation (*uppādanirodha-vāra*), reflecting an Abhidhamma metaphysics centered on experiential processes rather than substantial entities [Ronkin 2005].
While SuttaCentral records no curated external parallels for the text [SuttaCentral], DharmaNexus reveals extensive Pali-internal text reuse (18,151 matches across 48 texts), stemming from the Yamaka's repetitive, formulaic matrix [DharmaNexus]. Its closest reuse partners are its immediate counterparts within the *Sacca-yamaka*—the *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 5.2.2) and *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 5.2.3)—as well as the corresponding *Uppādavāra* sections of other Yamaka treatises, such as the *Indriyayamaka* (Ya 10.2.1), *Saṅkhārayamaka* (Ya 6.2.1), and *Anusayayamaka* (Ya 9.2.1), and canonical Abhidhamma subcommentaries like the *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages automatically with non-Pali scholastic literature, including Tibetan translations of Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* and Śamathadeva's *Tattvārthā*, as well as Sanskrit works such as the *Saṅghabhedavastu* and the *Arthaviniścayasūtra-nibandhana*, reflecting shared Abhidharma terminology rather than direct textual parallels [DharmaNexus].
